newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says he knows nothing of new file charges.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he knows nothing of new file charges.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Saturday he knew nothing about reports the White House sought FBI files on Republicans even after aides learned that they should not do so.

"I don't know anything about it other than what I saw in the paper today. I know nothing," Clinton told reporters in this western New York town where he was preparing for Sunday night's debate against Republican nominee Bob Dole.

Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Orrin Hatch, a Republican, said Senate documents released on Friday showed FBI files on hundreds of former Republican officials and aides were not obtained in a bureaucratic mistake as Clinton has said.

"My feeling is that somebody (at the White House) wanted to find dirt on these people either for current uses or uses at some time in the future," Hatch told reporters on Friday. "But to conclusively prove that at this point, we haven't been able to."
The White House Friday accused Hatch of playing politics less than five weeks before the Nov. 5 presidential election and said the Senate investigation proved no wrong-doing.
"Despite Mr. Hatch's partisan stunt, the bottom line remains clear: There is no indication that any FBI files were misused," White House aide Mark Fabiani said on Friday.
Allegations over the files, which the Clinton White House obtained on such prominent Republicans as former Secretary of State James Baker, have dogged Clinton for several months.
However, they do not seem to have had much of an impact on the electorate. National opinion polls show Clinton leads Dole by 10 to 20 percentage points.
